newsitem.title: CUBA: Castro meets Vatican foreign minister.
newsitem.headline: Castro meets Vatican foreign minister.

text.p: Cuban President Fidel Castro met visiting Vatican Foreign Minister Jean Louis Tauran late on Monday, diplomatic sources said.
The sources said Castro and Tauran, on a five-day visit to the communist-ruled island, met at the presidential palace in Havana.

Castro's talks with Tauran, who is the first Vatican foreign minister invited to Cuba by the government, reflected improved relations between the Cuban authorities and the Roman Catholic Church, and could be the prelude to a meeting between Castro and Pope John Paul.
Castro is expected to meet the pontiff if he travels to Rome for a U.N. summit on food from Nov. 13 to 17.
If the Cuban leader does meet the pope, diplomatic sources say he is likely to invite him to Cuba, the only country in Latin America the pontiff has not visited.

No details were available on what Tauran and Castro discussed in their talks, which continued late into the evening. But during his visit, which began last Friday, Tauran has called for a more public space for the Roman Catholic Church in Cuba.

He has cited the need for more flexibility in granting visas for foreign priests and nuns to work in the country, for the church to have access to the media and for the church charity Caritas to be allowed a wider field of work.

But Tauran has, at least in public, restricted his comments to the work of the church and has made no remarks about Cuba's political system. He has also pleased his hosts by condemning the longstanding U.S. embargo against Cuba.

Cuban officials are meanwhile anxious to stress there is currently a climate of mutual desire to improve church-state relations. Caridad Diego, head of the Communist Party's religious affairs department, told Tauran at the start of talks with him earlier on Monday she was sure problems in the relationship could be dealt with.
Tauran, who has also met Foreign Minister Roberto Robaina and parliamentary president Ricardo Alarcon as well as Cuban church leaders during his visit, was scheduled to leave Cuba on Tuesday.
